title: MATGEN-Q Phase 2 — Demonstrated Results & Scaling Boundary (verified, CPU)
pipeline: HamLib-format Hamiltonian (PySCF+OpenFermion, validated against published HamLib files) -> PennyLane -> two-stage GQE (generative structure discovery + continuous angle refinement)

scaling_boundary_cpu.description: Hamiltonian-expectation eval cost (lightning.qubit, single statevector eval) — the CPU bottleneck
scaling_boundary_cpu.growth: ~2100x eval-cost increase from 12 to 20 qubits, driven by exponential statevector dimension x growing Pauli-term count
scaling_boundary_cpu.implication: Exact statevector GQE training is CPU-bound at ~16 qubits. Reaching 20-40 qubits requires GPU acceleration + tensor-network (MPS) simulation.

resource_justification_phase3.bottleneck: Hamiltonian-expectation evaluation cost at scale (memory + term count). Exact statevector at 40q ~ 16 TB; infeasible.
request: NVIDIA A100 80GB or H100 GPUs with CUDA-Q SDK
tensornet-mps backend for 24-40 qubit tier (memory scales with entanglement, not 2^n)
cuStateVec exact for validation up to ~32 qubits
1 high-memory GPU sufficient for MPS; 4-8 GPUs (NVLink) for parallel circuit eval (Pillar 4) + >40q bonus attempt
qBraid platform access for hardware validation at 10-16 qubits
~2 weeks GPU wall-clock for pre-training + scaling sweep + benchmarking

validation: Hamiltonians verified term-for-term and spectrally against published HamLib files (ground-state agreement 0.00000 mHa for H2/H4/H6). HamLib contains no reference energies; FCI(<=20q)/CCSD(T)(<=40q) computed first-principles by our reproducible pipeline.
